item.title: 🔴 Our 2026 Cybersecurity Predictions: What We Got Right, What We Got Wrong, and What Changed
item.description:
Why this matters: Elevated ransomware risk — validate backups, endpoint protection, and recovery readiness.

Rapid7’s annual Security Predictions webinar returns on December 10, bringing our experts together to explore what the year ahead could hold for cybersecurity. Before sharing our predictions for 2027, we’re grading last year’s calls: that geopolitical tensions would reshape cyber threats, insider threats would dominate breach root causes, and context would become the new currency of cyber performance.

Register here for the 2027 Security Predictions webinar.

As security leaders work through their priorities for 2027, those predictions offer a useful starting point. The year reinforced several of the concerns we highlighted, while developments in attacker behavior and AI added new dimensions to the discussion. Looking at how those themes unfolded helps us understand what remains relevant and where our thinking needs to evolve.

Geopolitics shaped cyber targeting, with businesses caught in the middle

item.title: 🔴 Rapid7 Analysis: VMware vCenter SRP Authentication Bypass to Root (CVE-2026-123890)
item.description:
Why this matters: Credential/phishing risk — reinforce MFA and watch for suspicious sign-ins.

Overview

An unauthenticated attacker can retrieve the session key for an in-progress administrator login to VMware vCenter's directory service. The attacker then uses that key to complete the login without knowing the account's password. The vulnerable interface is exposed through DCE/RPC on TCP port 2012.

The issue, tracked as CVE-2026-123890, combines a Secure Remote Password (SRP) session-key getter that is callable before authentication with an RPC context lookup that does not enforce ownership. The context handles use predictable UUIDv1 values. By creating two reference contexts around a pending login, an attacker can narrow the hidden login handle to a short timestamp window and ask the server for its key.

We reproduced the bypass against vCenter Server Appliance 8.0.2.00400, build 23929136, running Photon OS 4.0, and leveraged the resulting administrator connection through to root command execution. SSH and Bash access were initially disabled. The attack recovered the directory databas…

item.title: 🔴 How exposure management can help public sector prepare for PHP2Shell-like vulnerabilities
item.description:
Why this matters: Credential/phishing risk — reinforce MFA and watch for suspicious sign-ins.

PHP2Shell showed how fast a runtime-level flaw can go from disclosure to confirmed exploitation. Here’s how federal, state, local, and education teams can prepare for PHP2Shell-like flaws.

Key takeaways

  1. PHP2Shell went from disclosure to confirmed exploitation within days. With AI shortening the disclosure-to-exploitation window, new critical flaws will likely move just as fast.
  2. Most security teams’ primary challenge with PHP2Shell was knowing where the vulnerabilities were in their environment. Teams that already knew where PHP ran across their IT infrastructure, web applications, and cloud assets were in a position to act quickly.
  3. Initial access flaws will continue to impact your network edge, so work backward from the foothold. Map what an attacker could reach after breaching an edge device, such as root access, management servers, and directory services. Then close those escalation paths by patching kernels and restricting unprivileged user namespaces.
  4. To prioritize, factor in exploitation evidence, not severity alone. Weigh KEV status, exploit prediction scores, and your own internet exposure, as well as pre-approve a plan for systems you can’t patch immediately.

item.title: 🔴 Metasploit Wrap Up: Breaking Zimbra's Identity Boundaries
item.description:
Why this matters: Credential/phishing risk — reinforce MFA and watch for suspicious sign-ins.

This release we have three pull requests from jburgess-r7 building out coverage for the identity-boundary issues detailed in Rapid7's Breaking Zimbra Identity Boundaries, Part One research.

First up is a new shared mixin, Msf::Exploit::Remote::HTTP::Zimbra, which gives every current and future Zimbra module a common foundation for account/admin SOAP authentication, canonical identity resolution, mailbox-server lookup, and version parsing, allowing future modules to stay focused on the vulnerability instead of re-implementing Zimbra's SOAP plumbing.

Built on top of that mixin are two new modules targeting CVEs from the same research track:

CVE-2026-73571 (#22080) It's an authorization bypass in Zimbra's SaveDraftRequest handling that lets an ordinary authenticated user send mail as another local mailbox without a delegation grant, landing a message in the victim's own Sent folder in the process.

item.description:

item.title: 🔴 NGINX2Root (CVE-2026-123007): Frequently asked questions about five critical NGINX vulnerabilities
item.description:
Why this matters: Remote-code-execution risk — assess exposure and patch or mitigate quickly.

Frequently asked questions about five critical NGINX remote code execution vulnerabilities and five additional flaws fixed in F5’s November 18 out-of-band release.

Change log

Update November 19: Added the Censys exposure data, test and lab reproductions and refined proof-of-concept details and added Tenable’s Vulnerability Watch classifications.

Click here to review the change log history

Update November 19: Added the Censys exposure data, test and lab reproductions and refined proof-of-concept details and added Tenable’s Vulnerability Watch classifications.

November 18: Initial publication.

Key takeaways

  1. NGINX2Root is associated with five critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities in NGINX, and a separate, unpatched Linux kernel local privilege escalation (LPE) flaw that can be chained with the NGINX bugs to gain root.
  2. CVE-2026-123007 is the most urgent of the five: an unauthenticated RCE flaw that requires only HTTP/2 to be enabled. A PoC is publicly available on GitHub but it is described as constrained, and on its own it runs code only as the NGINX worker.
